summary.intent: Investigate and fix extremely slow integration tests in the CLI repo, starting with a general performance analysis and then focusing on a specific test (TestAttach_AlreadyTracked_NoCheckpoint) that timed out at 9m15s for a coworker.
summary.outcome: Identified and fixed a bug where `promptAmendCommit` in `attach.go` called `huh.NewConfirm()` without checking `canPromptInteractively()`, causing the subprocess to hang indefinitely waiting for TTY input. The specific test dropped from 9m15s to 7s.

repo: The integration test suite builds the CLI binary once in TestMain (setup_test.go:25-26) before any tests run — this is a known serial bottleneck of ~30-60s.
Tests use ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0 env var to signal non-interactive mode, but this only works if the command code explicitly checks canPromptInteractively() before showing huh forms.
The established pattern for guarding interactive prompts is canPromptInteractively() — used correctly in setup.go and login.go but was missing in attach.go.
RunCLIWithError has no timeout; a hanging subprocess will run until the test framework's global timeout (default 10m) kills it.
217 tests exist, ~208 of which use t.Parallel(); the non-parallel ones are a secondary bottleneck worth investigating.

code.finding: promptAmendCommit called huh.NewConfirm() unconditionally without checking canPromptInteractively(), causing indefinite hangs in non-interactive (test) environments. Fixed by adding canPromptInteractively() guard that falls back to printing the copy-paste trailer.
RunCLI/RunCLIWithError helpers spawn subprocesses with no timeout, making them vulnerable to indefinite hangs if the subprocess blocks on interactive input.
Interactive PTY tests use 10-second time.After deadlines — these are safety nets, not the primary bottleneck.
Test called RunCLI('attach', ...) without -f flag, triggering the amend prompt path. Fixed by adding -f flag.

workflow: When a test hangs near the framework timeout (9m15s of a 10m limit), the root cause is almost always an unbounded subprocess block, not slow logic.
Grepping for huh.New(Confirm|Select|Input) is an effective way to audit all interactive prompt sites for missing canPromptInteractively() guards.
Running a single previously-hanging test with an explicit short timeout (e.g., 60s) is a fast way to verify a fix without running the full suite.

friction: The user interrupted the assistant mid-investigation (before non-parallel test analysis completed) to redirect toward the specific failing test — the initial broad investigation was partially wasted.
No timeout on RunCLIWithError means hanging subprocesses produce no actionable error; they silently consume the full test framework timeout before failing.
open_items: Broader audit of other commands (beyond attach.go) for huh form calls missing canPromptInteractively() guards — grep showed multiple sites not yet reviewed.

The initial performance investigation (binary build bottleneck, 218 subprocess-spawning tests, non-parallel tests) was deferred once the hanging test was identified — overall suite time of 134s has not been addressed.
RunCLIWithError should have a configurable or default timeout to prevent future hanging-subprocess test failures from burning the full 10m.
Non-parallel tests (~9 identified) should be reviewed to see if they can be parallelized.
